title: Mapping atypical UV photoproducts in vitro and across the S. cerevisiae genome
author: Bohm, Sivapragasam, et al.
materials: Timing: 3–4 h depending upon number of samples

steps.title: Observe radiation safety
steps.instruction: Wear a lab coat, goggles and gloves; perform all steps behind a certified radioactive shield; discard pipette tips in a radioactive waste container; avoid exposure to 32P beta rays.

steps.title: Label TA oligos and primers with 32P
steps.instruction: Combine annealed primers (2 µM final), 0.2 µCi ATPγ‑32P (1 µL), 10× PNK buffer (5 µL, 1× final), T4 polynucleotide kinase (0.2 U, 1 µL) and ddH₂O (42 µL) to a total volume of 50 µL. Incubate at 37 °C for 45 min then at 65 °C for 20 min to label the ‘TA’ oligos.

steps.title: Purify labelled primers with G‑50 columns
steps.instruction: Vortex a G‑50 Sephadex column at low speed, snip off the tip and open the cap ¼ turn. Place the column in a collection tube and centrifuge at 735 × g for 1 min (repeat if buffer remains). Add the labelled reaction to the centre of the resin without disturbing it and centrifuge at 735 × g for 2 min to elute DNA. Check radioactivity of the eluate with a Geiger‑Müller counter set to maximal sensitivity (100× or 10×).

steps.title: Label marker oligos with 32P
steps.instruction: In a 100 µL reaction mix add marker oligos OSS35, OSS33, OSS27 (17 µL each), OSS34 (20 µL), OSS28 (7 µL), OSS29‑OSS32 (17 µL each), 10× PNK buffer (10 µL), ATPγ‑32P (2 µL) and T4 polynucleotide kinase (2 µL). Incubate at 37 °C for 45 min then inactivate at 65 °C for 20 min.

steps.title: Purify labelled markers with G‑50 columns
steps.instruction: Purify the labelled marker oligos as described for primers using G‑50 columns. Because G‑50 columns do not efficiently elute oligos <20 nt, start with at least double the amount of the smaller markers. Load markers of similar size in separate wells if size differences cause overlapping bands.

steps.title: UVDE digestion and DNA preparation
steps.instruction: Digest UV‑treated DNA with UVDE and prepare samples for alkaline electrophoresis.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in 1 µL 10× UVDE buffer (pH 6.5) and 8 µL water; vortex and briefly centrifuge.
Add 1 µL UVDE enzyme, mix with a pipette and incubate at 55 °C for 1 h.
Add 50 µL TE buffer (pH 8), 60 µL phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (PCI) and 250 µL water; vortex 30 s.
Centrifuge 6 min at 16,873 × g; transfer 200 µL of the upper aqueous phase to a new tube.
Add 3 µL glycogen, 20 µL 3 M sodium acetate (pH 5.2) and 800 µL 100 % ethanol; invert to mix and store at –20 °C for ≥1 h (or up to 16 h).
Centrifuge 1 h at 16,873 × g; discard supernatant.
Add 1 mL 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 20 min at 16,873 × g, remove ethanol, perform a short spin to collect residual ethanol and remove it without touching the pellet.
Air‑dry the pellet 5–10 min behind the beta shield.
Resuspend in 6 µL water and 6 µL 100 % formamide; vortex and briefly centrifuge.
Heat at 95 °C for 10 min (use a heated‑lid or lid‑locker to prevent sample loss).

steps.title: Prepare glass plate assembly for gel
steps.instruction: Assemble the Sequi‑Gen GT glass plates for denaturing PAGE.

substeps.instruction: Lay the outer long and inner short IPC plates on a flat surface supported by two pipette‑tip boxes.
Wipe plates with water then ethanol; let dry.
Apply 2–3 drops of Rain‑X to one side of the outer long plate, spread evenly with a clean Kimwipe; remove excess.
Wipe 0.17 mm spacers with ethanol and place one on each side of the IPC plate.
Place the outer plate over the spacers, lift the assembly vertically, insert GT lever clamps on each side, and secure.
Insert the assembly into the precision caster base, adjust cam pegs, and lay the set‑up flat with the upper part raised a few inches (e.g., using a 15 mL tube).

steps.title: Cast 15 % denaturing urea PAGE gel
steps.instruction: Prepare and polymerize a 15 % polyacrylamide‑urea gel.

substeps.instruction: In a 200 mL beaker combine 26.25 mL 40 % acrylamide, 7 mL 10× TBE, 14.75 mL ddH₂O, 29.7 g urea; stir on a magnetic stirrer until urea dissolves.
Place the beaker on ice to keep the solution cold.
Just before casting, add 750 µL 10 % APS and 20 µL TEMED; mix gently, avoiding bubbles.
Draw the solution into a 60 mL syringe with a Luer taper, removing any bubbles.
Inject the solution slowly between the glass plates, insert the comb, and avoid air bubbles at the gel‑comb interface.
Allow the gel to polymerize for at least 1 h (up to 16 h). For longer storage, cover edges with wet 1× TBE‑soaked paper towel, wrap with saran wrap and store flat at 4 °C (max one week).

steps.title: Isolate genomic DNA from yeast
steps.instruction: Extract high‑quality gDNA from UV‑irradiated Saccharomyces cerevisiae.

substeps.instruction: Thaw cell pellet at 23 °C and rinse with ddH₂O.
Add 250 µL yeast lysis buffer, resuspend, and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube.
Add ~150 µL acid‑washed glass beads and 250 µL PCI (25:24:1, pH ≈ 6.7); vortex at maximum speed for 4 min (photolyase inactivated).
Add 200 µL TE buffer (pH 8) and vortex 1 min.
Centrifuge 10 min at ≥15,871 × g; transfer the clear aqueous phase to a fresh tube.
Add 1 mL cold 100 % ethanol, incubate 3–5 min at 23 °C, then centrifuge 3 min at ≥15,871 × g; discard supernatant.
Rinse pellet with 500 µL 75 % ethanol, centrifuge 3 min at ≥15,871 × g; remove ethanol, briefly spin to collect residual ethanol, and discard.
Air‑dry pellet ~5 min until ethanol evaporates.
Resuspend pellet in 200 µL TE (pH 8) by pipetting/vortexing.
Add 2 µL RNase A, mix, and incubate 37 °C for 30–60 min.
Add 200 µL PCI, vortex 30 s; add 200 µL TE, invert to mix; centrifuge 5 min at ≥15,871 × g.
Transfer aqueous layer to a new tube, add 1/10 total volume 3 M NaOAc, then 2 volumes cold 100 % ethanol; invert to mix.
Incubate at –20 °C for ≥15 min (preferably 16 h).
Centrifuge 30 min at 15,871 × g, 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 500 µL cold 75 % ethanol, centrifuge 5 min at 15,871 × g, 4 °C; remove supernatant, spin briefly, and air‑dry 5 min.
Resuspend final pellet in 310 µL ddH₂O.
If preparing a naked‑DNA library, expose the sample to UV‑C as described elsewhere.

steps.title: Prepare single‑stranded library
steps.instruction: Capture biotinylated DNA on streptavidin beads, wash, denature the non‑lesion strand, and precipitate the single‑strand.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL Dynabeads M‑280 Streptavidin to a fresh 1.5 mL tube; place on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add 1 mL 1× bind‑and‑wash buffer, vortex briefly, centrifuge briefly, place on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add 40 µL 2× bind‑and‑wash buffer, vortex briefly, centrifuge briefly, place on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add the DNA sample (entire 40 µL volume) to the beads, vortex briefly, rotate at 23 °C for 15 min, then place on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add 50 µL 1× saline‑sodium citrate (SSC), vortex briefly, rotate 10 min, place on magnet and discard supernatant.
Add 40 µL 0.15 M NaOH, vortex briefly, rotate 10 min at 23 °C, place on magnet and transfer the supernatant (contains the single‑strand) to a new tube.
Repeat the NaOH capture once more and pool the eluates.
To the pooled eluate add 120 µL ddH₂O, 2 µL glycogen, 20 µL 3 M NaOAc (pH 5.2) and 550 µL cold 100 % ethanol; flick to mix after each addition.
Incubate at –20 °C for ≥12 h (or overnight).

steps.title: Perform bioinformatic analysis
steps.instruction: Process sequencing reads to map TA lesions genome‑wide.

substeps.instruction: Separate reads by the 6‑nt barcode (A1–A6) and trim the barcode from each FASTQ file.
Align reads to the SacCer3 genome with Bowtie2: `bowtie2 -x saccer3 -U <fastq> -S <sam>`.
Convert SAM to BAM: `samtools view -b -S <sam> > <bam>`.
Convert BAM to BED: `bedtools bamtobed -i <bam> > <bed>`.
Locate the damage site on the opposite strand (adjust coordinates ±2 bp depending on strand) using the provided Perl script.
Extract the dinucleotide sequence at each damage site: `bedtools fastaFromBed -s -name -fi saccer3_genome.fa -bed <damage.bed> -fo <damage.fasta>`.
Count occurrences of each dinucleotide using the supplied Perl counting script.
Filter the counts to retain only TA lesions with the provided Perl filter script.
Plot the final TA‑lesion frequencies (e.g., with GraphPad Prism).

description: Here we describe a protocol that utilizes the recently discovered ability of UVDE to cleave atypical ‘TA’ UV lesions. The in vitro section of the protocol validates UVDE cleavage of ‘TA’ photoproducts in oligonucleotides, and the in vivo UVDE-seq section of the protocol uses UVDE to map atypical photoproducts throughout the Saccharomyces cerevisiae genome (Figure 1). This protocol may be modified for use in other organisms or cell lines.Figure 1In vitro and in vivo ‘TA’ photoproduct cleavage protocol overview CRITICAL: Appropriate safety protocol has to be followed while handling radioactive material. Wear Lab coat, goggles and gloves. Each step is performed behind the shield without accidently getting exposed to the beta rays of 32P ideally in a radioactive certified hood. Discard the pipette tips carefully into a radioactive waste container.
